summary: This repo contains an AFOQT study app. Copilot must auto-generate Instrument Comprehension (IC) beginner JSON files using a simple profile list and a Node.js generator script.
goals: Generate two JSON files for Instrument Comprehension beginner level: instrument_comprehension_beginner_part1.json and instrument_comprehension_beginner_part2.json.
Each part must contain exactly 25 questions (ic_b1_001–ic_b1_025 for part 1, ic_b1_026–ic_b1_050 for part 2).
Each question defines an instrument panel and four airplane image choices (choiceSprites A–D); only A is correct.
Use a small JavaScript generator (Node.js) to build these JSON files from a simple list of flight profiles.

questionSchema.description: All IC beginner questions must match this JSON structure.

fields.copilotInstruction: Short description telling the renderer to draw an attitude indicator and compass matching the uiSpec values and to use choiceSprites A–D as aircraft images.
fields.question: String; phrased as: 'Which airplane best matches the instruments (DESCRIPTION)?'
fields.answer: Always 'A' for generated questions (Copilot may adjust later if distractor logic changes).
fields.explanation: Text explaining that the correct airplane matches bank, pitch, and heading.
steps: Step-by-step solution using C1-style tutoring: read bank, read pitch, read heading, compare planes, pick the one matching all three.
fields.fastStrategy: Short heuristic: e.g., 'Match heading first to cut options, then match bank direction and pitch.'

constraints: A’s choiceSprites entry must exactly match artificialHorizon.bankDegrees, artificialHorizon.pitchDegrees, and compass.headingDegrees.
B, C, and D must each be plausible but wrong by exactly one dimension (wrong heading, wrong bank, or wrong pitch).

Beginner attitudes should be simple: moderate banks (~10–30 degrees), moderate pitch (~5–15 degrees up/down), and standard headings (cardinal and diagonal headings like 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315).

profileSchema.description: Copilot should drive generation from a small 'profiles' array, where each profile = one question.

fields.bankDegrees: number; positive = right bank, negative = left bank, 0 = wings level.
fields.pitchDegrees: number; positive = climb, negative = descent, 0 = level.
fields.view: string; e.g., 'side', 'front', 'oblique'; determines how to draw the jet.
fields.correctSpriteId: string; base sprite name for the correct airplane image.
fields.description: string; human-readable description used in the question text (e.g., 'climbing right turn toward the northeast').

example.description: climbing right turn toward the northeast

copilotTasks: When working in files related to Instrument Comprehension, prefer modifying the generator script and profiles array instead of hand-editing large JSON blocks.
Ensure every generated question respects the questionSchema: exactly one correct airplane (A) and three plausible distractors (B, C, D) that differ by only one of heading, bank, or pitch.
Keep beginner attitudes simple and readable: avoid extreme angles; use clean increments (10, 20, 30 degrees; headings at 0/45/90/135/180/225/270/315).
When the user adds or edits a profile, update the corresponding JSON via the generator script rather than manual editing.
